chapter: Grievances over Bolden, Bunk Johnson and Black bands
title: La Rocca on Armand Hug, Buddy Bolden and Bunk Johnson
summary: La Rocca dismisses Hug and says the Jazz Club invented Bolden stories and 'resurrected' Bunk Johnson.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Almond Hug with regards with regards with what has been said. Arm and Hug being a young man, I didn't think it was the right thing for me to do to contact this boy because this program was put on by the WDSU programming department. And all this was all mapped out and planned before they went on the air what was to say. Furthermore, if you took the Dixieland Licks away from Arm and Hug, he wouldn't even play piano because that's all he plays, Dixieland Licks, to embellish his music with. There's a man probably 40 years old, maybe not that old, talking on jazz, history of jazz. That's the kind of people you have around New Orleans that elaborate on something they know nothing about. Probably he did hear Negroes play. But maybe before the Negroes played, there must have been other men playing this music too. He didn't hear them because he's going by something that was told what to say. And that can only come from the New Orleans Jazz Club, who were writing for Negro stories at this time. They wrote about Mr. Glennie. I never heard of Mr. Glennie. They wrote about Buddy Bolden. They wrote about Buddy Bolden. They had this man, Tom Sanction, from the Island to go up to the crazy house to find out if he ever played music up there, what he did. They wrote great big articles about him in the paper, all propaganda. Nobody heard of Bullen, but Bullen was a great cornet player. They started digging the graves to find out if he had the cornet down there with him and if he could come back and play a little piece for him like they had Bunk Johnson. After 30 years of hearing this music, they resurrected Bunk Johnson, a man by the name of Allen. I don't know whether he's in relation to you, Mr. Allen, or...
No, I never... I don't know who this man is, but this is before my time.
